headline: UK arrests 3 over fake gay asylum claims involving Bangladeshis
summary: Suspects allegedly charged up to £4,500 for fabricated evidence to help Bangladeshi men obtain protection in the UK.
details: The UK has arrested three people linked to a network accused of helping asylum seekers make false claims about being gay to obtain protection.
Two suspects were arrested at London addresses on Tuesday on suspicion of fraud and immigration offences, while a third was detained for suspected illegal residence.
The suspects are believed to have helped dozens of Bangladeshi men submit asylum claims by providing fabricated evidence, including false letters, certificates, and staged photographs.
The Home Office investigation involves false claims linked to Aponjon, a Bangladeshi LGBT organisation in east London, with over 100 related asylum applications now under review.
Immigration judges have previously criticised evidence from Aponjon as unreliable, including cases where applicants submitted staged photographs of group events.
The arrests follow a BBC investigation that revealed some legal firms and advisers were helping migrants pretend to be gay in asylum applications.
Home Secretary Shabana Mahmood warned that those profiting from fraudulent asylum claims will face prosecution and asset seizure.
Convictions for asylum fraud in the UK can lead to up to 10 years in prison.
caption:
Charging up to £4,500 for fake evidence, a network in the UK has been busted for helping Bangladeshi men fake gay asylum claims.

The UK has arrested three people linked to a network accused of helping asylum seekers make false claims about being gay to obtain protection.

Two suspects were arrested at London addresses on Tuesday on suspicion of fraud and immigration offences, while a third was detained for suspected illegal residence.

The suspects are believed to have helped dozens of Bangladeshi men submit asylum claims by providing fabricated evidence, including false letters, certificates, and staged photographs.

The Home Office investigation involves false claims linked to Aponjon, a Bangladeshi LGBT organisation in east London, with over 100 related asylum applications now under review.

Immigration judges have previously criticised evidence from Aponjon as unreliable, including cases where applicants submitted staged photographs of group events.

The arrests follow a BBC investigation that revealed some legal firms and advisers were helping migrants pretend to be gay in asylum applications.

Home Secretary Shabana Mahmood warned that those profiting from fraudulent asylum claims will face prosecution and asset seizure.

Convictions for asylum fraud in the UK can lead to up to 10 years in prison.

headline: 3 jailed after posing as CID officers to extort 1 million BDT from jewelry shop
summary: The suspects entered a gold shop in Old Dhaka, threatening the owner's family with hundi business allegations to demand money.
details: A Dhaka court has sent three men to jail for allegedly posing as Criminal Investigation Department (CID) officers to extort 1 million BDT from a jewelry shop in Tantibazar, Old Dhaka.
caption:
Posing as CID officers, three men tried to extort 1 million BDT from a jewelry shop owner in Old Dhaka.
